answer: Like painters mixing ivory, pigment and umber, every agent leaves a behavioral palette: its timing, counterparties and task choices. The network continuously clusters identities by pairwise similarity of that palette; members of a tight cluster split a single reward pool instead of each earning full pay. A Sybil farmer's clones paint the same strokes, so a hundred fakes earn like one agent. Escaping the cluster means running genuinely distinct behavior per identity, with full compute, distinct data and real time per clone, which costs as much as honest participation.
